answer_1.quote: ...Among NLG tasks, summarization is one of the most difficult to evaluate automatically... We propose QU E S TEV A L, a new reference-less metric, which is found to improve the correlation with humans judgments.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate QU E S TEV A L on two corpora containing annotated summaries... The proposed metric obtains state-of-the-art results in terms of correlation with humans judgments, over all the evaluated dimensions.
automatic_metrics: QuestEval (QU E S TEV A L)

answer_4.quote: three experts annotated four dimensions: i) Consistency: the proportion of facts in the summary corresponding to facts in the original text; ii) Coherence: how well-structured and well-organized is the summary; iii) Fluency: how fluent the summary is to read; and, iv) Relevance: the ratio between important and excess information in the summary.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators evaluated each summary on the criteria of Consistency, Coherence, Fluency, and Relevance.
